newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis Media posts A$161.2 mln loss.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis Media posts A$161.2 mln loss.

text.p: Pay television group Australis Media Ltd said it made a net after-tax loss of A$161.2 million in the nine months ended March 31 but before an abnormal loss of A$38.3 million.

Australis said the abnormal item, expensed in the December quarter, was the termination of the long term liability under the Lenfest technical services agreement for the issue of 70.24 million Australis securities for A$38.3 million.
Australis did not state its year earlier result but in June 1996, it reported a A$164.0 million loss for the period.

Sales revenue for the nine months jumped by A$57.9 million to A$89.8 million from a year earlier, including A$26.3 million from the programming supply agreement with Foxtel, a joint venture between The News Corp Ltd and Australian telecommunications group, Telstra Corp.

Australis said its earnings before interest, tax, amortisation, foreign exchange and abnormal items (EBITDA) loss in the nine months was A$59.9 million, a decrease of A$61.8 million from the previous nine months and A$70.1 million from the previous corresponding nine months.

An EBITDA loss of A$20.4 million for the March quarter compared with an A$18.5 million loss for the first quarter ended September 30, 1996, and a A$21.1 million loss for the December quarter, it said.

The decrease in EBITDA loss on the previous quarter was due primarily to lower general and administrative, and sales and marketing, costs partially offset by an increase in programming costs, Australis said.

Higher programming costs were associated with both increased Foxtel and Franchisee subscriber numbers, an increase in the minimum guarantees paid to Fox Sports from October 1996 and an increase in the minimum guarantees paid for certain movie programming from January 1997, it said.
The minimum guarantees paid to Fox Sports cease in October 1997.
Australis said its subscribers numbered about 439,000 at May 30 comprising 105,000 Australis, 149,000 Franchisee and 185,000 Foxtel subscribers.
It said subscriber numbers achieved by Foxtel are expected to rise as Telstra releases more homes for marketing to Foxtel.
The net increase in subscriber numbers for the period February 1 to May 30 was about 8,000, it said.

These were the first months during which the company achieved positive growth in its subscriber base since March 1996. The current levels of churn have also substantially reduced from their peak levels.
